'''Vladimir Isaakovich Minkin''' ({{langx|ru|Владимир Исаакович Минкин}}; born 4 March 1935, [[Rostov-on-Don]]) is a [[Russians|Russian]] [[chemist]]. [[Professor]], [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Chemical Sciences]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ras.ru/win/db/show_per.asp?P=.id-1179.ln-ru.dl-.pr-inf.uk-12|title=Минкин В.И. - Общая информация|website=www.ras.ru|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Vladimir Isaakovich Minkin graduated from the Chemical Faculty of [[Rostov State University]] in 1957. Since 1967 he was a Professor of the Department of Natural Compounds, in 1981-2012 — Director of the Research Institute of Physical Organic Chemistry of the RSU ([[Southern Federal University|SFedU]]). Since 2003 he was Vice-Chairman of the Southern Scientific Center of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], in 2004-2009 — head of the Department of Natural and High-Molecular Compounds of the [[Southern Federal University]]. Since 2012 — scientific supervisor of SFedU.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ipoc.sfedu.ru/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=110|title=IPOC - Минкин Владимир Исаакович|website=www.ipoc.sfedu.ru|access-date=2018-05-12|archive-date=2018-05-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180513080913/http://www.ipoc.sfedu.ru/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=110|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Corresponding Member of the [[USSR Academy of Sciences]] since 1990, full member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] since 1994 (Department of General and Technical Chemistry).<ref name=":0" /> Member of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (1994).<ref name=":1" />

His main works are devoted to physical [[Organic chemistry|organic]] and [[quantum chemistry]]. He studied the structure and molecular dynamics of organic and [[organometallic]] compounds.

In 1974 he discovered (together with [[Lev Olekhnovich]] and [[Yuri Zhdanov]]) the phenomenon of acylotrophy — rapid reversible migration of acyl groups between [[nucleophilic]] centers in [[organic molecules]].<ref>Минкин В. И., Олехнович Л. П., Жданов Ю. А. Явление ацилотропии. Диплом на открытие № 146, 1974 г. [[Государственный реестр открытий СССР]], 1975.</ref> He was the founder of a new scientific field — chemistry of structurally nonrigid molecules in the ground and excited states. He developed the theory of orbital stabilization of "nonclassical" structures of organic compounds.<ref>[[Гарновский, Александр Дмитриевич|Гарновский А. Д.]] Владимир Исаакович Минкин // [[Российский химический журнал]]. 1996. Т. XL. № 4-5. С. 196—198.</ref> He also studied [[tautomerism]] and [[photochromism]] of organic compounds, stereodynamics of coordination compounds, nonclassical organic and elementorganic structures, bistable molecular systems with light-controlled reversible rearrangements.<ref name=":1" />

In 1999 he was the writer of the final draft, (but not the only chemist beyond this new gold standards: the cooperation between researchers was the key of this achievement) which is the "Glossary of terms used in theoretical organic chemistry" <ref>Pure and Applied Chemistry, vol. 71, no. 10, 1999, pp. 1919-1981.</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://doi.org/10.1351/pac199971101919 | doi=10.1351/pac199971101919 | title=Glossary of terms used in theoretical organic chemistry | year=1999 | last1=Minkin | first1=V. I. | journal=Pure and Applied Chemistry | volume=71 | issue=10 | pages=1919–1981 | s2cid=6475517 | doi-access=free }}</ref>

He is a member of the editorial board of such journals as "Advances in Heterocyclic Chemistry", "Mendeleev Communications", "[[Russian Chemical Reviews]]", "Journal of General Chemistry", "Journal of Organic Chemistry" and so on. He is also the author of 12 monographs and more than 800 articles in both Russian and foreign journals. Currently he is of the most cited Russian scientists.<ref>[http://expertcorps.ru/science/whoiswho/ci86 Список российских учёных, имеющих свыше 1000 цитирований по ISI]</ref>

Laureate of [[USSR State Prize]] (1989). LXII [[Mendeleev readings|Mendeleev reader]] (2006).<ref name=":1" />
